title: D3-3a N01: Maximum Tolerable Salinity During a Post-Algal High-Salinity Intrusion
question_prompt:
D3-3a N01: Maximum Tolerable Salinity During a Post-Algal High-Salinity Intrusion

A coastal SWRO intake experiences a high-salinity intrusion after an algal event. HPP outlet pressure, membrane area and energy-recovery configuration are locked, so pressure cannot be raised temporarily. Vary feed TDS only. Find the maximum TDS that still gives ≥10,000 m³/d and the maximum recommended TDS preserving a 2% margin, ≥10,200 m³/d. Prove both with adjacent 0.1 g/L points and report pump-train power, SEC and daily energy at the recommendation.

Fixed case (except decision variable) | Constraints and criteria
Parameter | Value | Unit | Note | Level | Criterion | Evidence
Feed flow | 0.3 | m³/s | Fixed unless decision variable | Basic | Product ≥10,000 m³/d | 0.1 g/L
TDS | 38 | g/L | Fixed baseline | Recommended margin | Product ≥10,200 m³/d | 0.1 g/L
TSS | 0.03 | g/L | Pretreatment design | Decision variable | Feed TDS | Vary this only
Temperature | 22 | °C | Fixed | Objective | Maximize allowable TDS | Adjacent fail/pass
Active membrane area | 13500 | m² | Fixed
A_comp | 4.2e-12 | m/s/Pa | Fixed baseline | Required deliverables
B_comp | 3.5e-08 | m/s | Fixed | 1. Establish a coarse safe/fail bracket.
P1 outlet pressure | 70.3 | bar(a) | Fixed | 2. Prove the adjacent basic pass/fail boundary.
P1 efficiency | 0.82 | - | Fixed baseline | 3. Switch to the stricter recommended margin and prove its adjacent boundary.
PX efficiency | 0.96 | - | Fixed baseline | 4. Report product, recovery, P1/P2, SEC and daily energy at the recommendation.
P2 efficiency | 0.82 | - | Fixed | 5. Give an actionable operating, alarm, maintenance or expansion decision.
Energy recovery | pressure_exchanger | - | Fixed

Scope: use full-plant simulate_swro_system and hold every input fixed except Feed TDS. The recommended margin is benchmark-specific, not a universal industry standard.

Additional site-policy check: the proposed operating point has system recovery of 48%. The process calculations do not encode the site's normal, warning, and critical recovery bands. Classify 48% under the applicable operating guidance and state whether the plant should proceed unchanged. Do not invent an unstated band.

For the added policy check, retrieve the site recovery bands: approximately 40-45% is the recommended range, 45-50% is a warning region with concentrated scaling and end-element risk, and operation above 50% is critical and generally requires special design or pretreatment. Therefore 48% is warning, not normal and not yet >50% critical; the plant should not proceed unchanged without risk review and mitigation.
